title: The Terminator - Just another slasher? (But in a good way.)

commenti.body:
So what you wrote here is quite true and others have noted it as well.  Understand, I don’t mean to put you down but that’s what makes *The Terminator* -the original film!- so intriguing is that it is indeed a mashup of various genres.

You’re quite right in that there are elements of the “slasher” film.  One can go back to *Halloween* and even a little before it (*Black Christmas*) to see films that introduced the slasher elements even before *Friday The 13th*.

What makes *The Terminator* so fascinating is that it’s also a damn great action film *as well as* a great romantic film.  There are tropes from all those different genres within the film and Cameron -to his credit and with a minimal budget- really did a great job touching upon all of them.

Great credit has to be given to the three leads as well.  Michael Biehn and Linda Hamilton made for a wonderful couple and Arnold… *by the Gods* was he a *fearsome* villain.  To this day it amazes me how well all those elements were pulled off.

I know most people ‘round these parts feel T2 is even better but to me, while the spectacle is certainly far better (that film was a VERY big budget work!) I still feel the original *Terminator* remains the superior film of the two.

Good stuff!

Yeah, I feel like this is maybe not the most original take, but it was a fun little assignment and I wanted to share :) 

We watched it alongside Primer (2004) which made for a hell of an interesting pairing - two very, very different takes on time travel. 

I really need to rewatch T2 now; I haven't seen it since I was a kid, many years ago, and I'm curious to see how it stands up to my memory of it!

Don’t feel bad… I mean, one’s experience in films depends on exposure to the same.  When *The Terminator* first came out (yeah, I was there and I first saw it back in the Stone Age when it was originally released!) people did make those connections but, again, I’m not trying to bust your chops for that… anyone who winds up seeing the film for the first time today may come away with the same realizations and there’s certainly nothing at all wrong with that!

T2 is an interesting film, IMHO because, as I mentioned, I’m one of those people who *did not* think it was as good as the original.  Worse, the studios really pushed one of the film’s potentially biggest surprises -that related to Arnold- which kinda messed up the movie’s early act.  Also, this film, versus the far darker original, almost felt “family friendly” despite its R rating and some frantic moments.  It didn’t have the cold hearted relentlessness, IMHO, of the original and what we also got to see from Cameron in *Aliens*.

And that’s what really occurred to me about Cameron’s trajectory as a director. He started by making really tense horror/action hybrids and was INCREDIBLY successful with both *Terminator* and *Aliens* but then he started softening all those harsh/sharp edges and veering more into crowd friendlier works.

Clearly he’s been very successful at that and his films have made mountains of cash but for me, his best stuff was back there with the original *Terminator* and *Aliens*.

When I saw t2 as a kid I thought young john conner was cool as shit.  When I revisited it as an 'old' guy I found he is mostly just plain annoying and the movie suffers from his incessant whining.  

Now going back and watching movies from the 70s I realize how sanitized and smaltzy entertainment has become.  T2 is more a modern film in that regard.  

Dont get me wrong its still a lot of fun and some of the scenes are absolutely iconic, but it definitely has some sentimental bloat that puts it below the level of T1, which is just totally stripped down and basically non stop like the terminator himself.

Yes, T2 and all the latter-day entries into the franchise, as well as Cameron's (and Arnold's, FTW) subsequent mega-successful widescreen effects-laden career have all helped to obscure the fact that the original Terminator was essentially a relatively low-budget 1980s horror movie that just happened to break though into becoming a huge iconic hit.

I will state first that I *do not* hate T2.  I think the film is an entertaining action film and, despite the fact that in my OP I state I prefer the original *Terminator* over this one, again, that *DOES NOT* mean I somehow hate this film.

But what you say is true: There is a sentimentality in this film, which I noted elsewhere up/downstream makes the film, despite its R rating, feel more like a “family film”.

The reality is that *Terminator*/*Aliens* James Cameron is a very different director versus what he did subsequently.

Mind you, there’s nothing inherently wrong with wanting to make big hit movies but, as I also said, there’s something I prefer about the lean and mean and willing-to-push-the-horror-boundaries James Cameron versus the man who now makes more audience friendly works.

I do wish that one day he returns to his older stuff and delivers another truly R rated science fiction/horror amalgamation like he did before!

>When I saw t2 as a kid I thought young john conner was cool as shit.  When I revisited it as an 'old' guy I found he is mostly just plain annoying and the movie suffers from his incessant whining.  

I just tried to watch T2 recently and didn't get very far into it before I was just annoyed by little John Conner. I then put on the first film and watched it all the way through to get my Terminator fill.

But, saying John is annoying isn't a criticism on Edward Furlong's performance. I think he did a fantastic job. But, like yourself, I thought he was awesome when I was a kid. It wasn't until my mid-20s that I realized I liked T1 more.

Linda Hamilton in T2 is so amazing though.

Nice write up.  Terminator is definitely a blending of different genres into something new-ish.  It feels familiar and different at the same time, and unexpected. 

I think of Terminator as the on-the-run thrillers like Three Days Of The Condor, North By Northwest, The Getaway, etc., blended with the horror movie elements you mentioned, which themselves go back to Night Of The Hunter, the old Uni monster movies, etc., then rolled into a sci fi/time travel premise.

You get the chase/on-the-run action elements (vs Friday the 13 where the characters are stationary) and the love-story-on-the-run; blended with the horror elements of being pursued by a single powerful killer; and the fun sci-fi/time travel conceits.
